judge.delivered_result: A stepwise 31P NMR account claiming: POCl3 singlet at +35 to +48 ppm; monoalkyl phosphorodichloridate at +10 to +25 ppm; dialkyl phosphorochloridate as a single signal at ~0 to +10 ppm; final dialkylphosphate at 0 to -5 ppm with 'one or two peaks' depending on whether the diastereomers happen to be resolved.
judge.correct_result: POCl3 resonates near +4 to +5 ppm; the monoalkyl phosphorodichloridate (P not stereogenic) gives one singlet; after addition of the second enantiopure chiral alcohol phosphorus becomes a stereocenter, so the dialkyl phosphorochloridate exists as two diastereomers giving two singlets; hydrolysis retains the P stereocenter, so over the final reaction the two chloridate singlets are replaced by two new singlets of the diastereomeric dialkylphosphate product.
